# Yousef Eid Abdelmongy

> Personal portfolio of Yousef Eid Abdelmongy, a machine learning engineer and Computer Science student based in Cairo, Egypt. He builds machine learning models, web platforms and ERP systems, completed the DEPI Machine Learning Engineer track, and founded ScaleForce.

## Main page

- [Portfolio home](https://yousefeid.tech/): About, machine learning and data skills, web and ERP projects, work experience, education and certifications, articles, and contact details (email, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, GitHub).
- [النسخة العربية](https://yousefeid.tech/ar.html): Arabic version of the portfolio homepage.

## Project case studies

- [Gold Price Analysis & Prediction](https://yousefeid.tech/gold-price-prediction.html): Machine learning case study - predicting gold prices from 2017-2025 data with Lasso Regression tuned by GridSearchCV; feature engineering (moving averages, daily returns, lag features); evaluated with RMSE, MAE and R-squared. Python, Pandas, scikit-learn.
- [ERP System for Al Nokhba Stone](https://yousefeid.tech/al-nokhba-erp.html): Browser-based ERP for a marble and granite company - 17 modules and 11 roles covering purchasing, block and slab inventory, manufacturing, export orders, CRM, invoicing, accounting and HR; Arabic RTL dashboard; no backend (localStorage).
- [Tech Career Roadmap Platform](https://yousefeid.tech/tech-career-roadmap.html): EdTech web platform that helps CS students choose their tech track with organized learning tracks, roadmaps and curated free resources; he led the team and delivered the first working prototype.

## Articles

- [How I Built a Gold Price Prediction Model with Python](https://yousefeid.tech/how-i-built-gold-price-prediction-model.html): First-person story of his first full ML workflow - cleaning the DOJI gold price daily dataset (2017-2025), feature engineering with MA_7, MA_30, Daily_Return and lag features, Lasso Regression tuned with GridSearchCV, evaluated with RMSE, MAE and R-squared.
- [5 Mistakes I Made in My First Machine Learning Project](https://yousefeid.tech/first-ml-project-mistakes.html): Honest lessons - a KeyError on the date column, a missing target column, one-hot encoding that exploded the data to 5,105 columns, the drop_duplicates trap in time series, and guessing hyperparameters instead of searching.
